keypoints.name: Newton's Third Law
keypoints.description: Explains lift as a reaction to the wing deflecting air downwards. The equal and opposite reaction provides an upward force (lift).
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Dedicated section with clear examples (boat, rocket). Mentions its role in explaining lift.

keypoints.name: Bernoulli's Principle
keypoints.description: Explains lift as a consequence of pressure differences created by airflow over the wing. Higher velocity air has lower pressure, contributing to an upward force.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Dedicated section, example of air nozzle, links to lift generation, reviewed and summarized.
representative_quotes: as the velocity of a fluid increases, the pressure of that fluid decreases and vice versa
pressure below the wing is greater than the pressure above the wing

keypoints.name: Airfoil and Angle of Attack
keypoints.description: The shape of the wing (airfoil) and its angle relative to the oncoming air (angle of attack) determine how air is split and pressure is distributed, leading to lift.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Covered in the explanation of lift, but not a standalone section. Shown in a diagram. Summarized at end.
